newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end shade higher, still volatile.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end shade higher, still volatile.

text.p: Argentine stocks showed a slight rise at the close Tuesday after stronger earlier gains were thwarted by a fresh Wall Street dive, dealers said.

"The market tried to perform an upwards correction, aided by rising cash flows and a stable U.S. long bond yield," said Emilio Alessandro at brokers Alessandro. "But the rise was undermined by the sharp drop in the Dow and tomorrow should be another volatile session."
The weighted MerVal index rose 0.6 percent to 706.47, after falling 1.3 percent Monday and 2.6 percent last week.
"I think the MerVal will drift within a range of 690-720 between now and next Tuesday (when the U.S. Federal Reserve meets to discuss interest rates)," another trader said.
However, if Wednesday's U.S. consumer inflation data does not match expectations and spooks the markets, "then we could see the bolsa slip through its support levels."
Floor volume picked up to 19.4 million pesos from 15 million Monday, while over-the-counter deals slowed to 134.6 million from 156.2 million Monday.
The broad market closed up 0.7 percent, with risers beating losers 38 to 14 and 19 stocks closing flat.
Best main-tier performers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which tacked on 3.3 percent, and oil company Astra and construction stock Polledo, both up 2.9 percent.
Losers were led by carmaker Ciadea, which traders said tumbled 4.8 percent on looming management changes and an apparent trend of lower production and higher imports.
Textile and footwear firm Alpargatas fell 1.1 percent and petrochemical concern Indupa shed 0.9 percent.
